# Configuration reference

Rimsky reads three kinds of configuration file. This page lists every key in each one, its type, its default, and what it does.

| File | Who reads it | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rimsky.yml` | every rimsky role process and the migrate step | `/etc/rimsky/rimsky.yml`, or the path in `RIMSKY_CONFIG` |
| CLI config | the `rimsky` CLI | `~/.rimsky/config.yml` |
| CLI service aliases | the `rimsky` CLI | `~/.rimsky/aliases.yml` and `./.rimsky/aliases.yml` |

Each bundled claim producer reads its own file, named by its own environment variable. Publisher configuration is not a file at all: it lives in the template, under `publishers[].config`. Both are covered below.

## How every file is read

All three files, and both bundled-producer files, go through one loader with one behaviour.

**Unknown keys stop the process.** The loader decodes strictly. A typo, a guess, a stale example, or a retired key fails at load, and the error names the offending field. A container that will not start because you wrote `persistance` is the loader working as designed.

**`${VAR}` references expand from the process environment.** Write `${DB_PASSWORD}` anywhere in the file and the loader substitutes the environment value at load time. A referenced variable that is not set is a hard error naming the variable, not an empty string.

**There is no per-key environment override.** Guessing a variable name from a key path — `RIMSKY_PERSISTENCE_DRIVER`, `RIMSKY_EXECUTORS_FOO_ENDPOINT` — changes nothing and warns about nothing: the deployment comes up on the file's values as though you had set no variable at all. The product checks the values of the fixed set of variables it knows and never checks the names of variables it does not, so an environment typo is silent where the same typo in YAML is loud. To configure a container from the environment, put `${VAR}` references in the file and set those variables.

## rimsky.yml

Fourteen top-level keys. `persistence` is the only required one.

### persistence

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `persistence.driver` | `postgres` \| `sqlite` | none — required | Selects the database. Any other value fails at load. |
| `persistence.postgres.dsn` | string | none — required under `postgres` | The Postgres connection string. |
| `persistence.postgres.max_open_conns` | int | driver default | Caps the connection pool. Ignored at 0. |
| `persistence.postgres.min_conns` | int | driver default | Floor on idle pooled connections. Ignored at 0. |
| `persistence.postgres.conn_max_lifetime` | duration | driver default | Retires a pooled connection after this age. Ignored at 0. |
| `persistence.sqlite.path` | absolute path | none — required under `sqlite` | The database file. A relative path fails at load. |

The `postgres:` and `sqlite:` blocks are mutually exclusive; declaring the block that does not match `driver`, or omitting the one that does, fails at load.

Durations are Go duration strings: `30s`, `5m`, `1h`, `720h`.

**A SQLite deployment warns at every boot that the driver is for local development only.** The graph behaviour matches the Postgres driver's — the same template produces the same events, node runs, frames, and read-route shapes on either driver — so a development run on SQLite does reproduce a Postgres run. Outside the single-process all-in-one, a SQLite deployment warns further: every role process and every replica must share one local, non-network database file, and nothing inside a process can detect a deployment that fails to provide one.

### claim_producers

A map of operator-chosen name to producer entry. The name is opaque to rimsky: no code path treats an entry differently for naming a particular implementation.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claim_producers.<name>.endpoint` | `host:port`, optionally `grpc://host:port` | none — required | Where to dial the producer. An `http://`, `https://`, `tcp://`, or `unix://` prefix is rejected. |
| `claim_producers.<name>.write_semantics_allowed` | list of `sync` \| `staged_async` \| `blocking_async` \| `read_only` | none — required | Narrows what this producer may realize. Must be a subset of the producer's advertised set; a superset fails at startup. |
| `claim_producers.<name>.tls` | `off` \| `required` | `off`, or `required` when `service_auth: mtls` | `required` verifies the service's server certificate. |
| `claim_producers.<name>.protocols` | list | `[claim_producer]` | Which protocols this service speaks. Must include `claim_producer`. |
| `claim_producers.<name>.observability_endpoint` | `host:port` | the entry's `endpoint` | Address of the service's observability protocol when it is served separately. |

The legal protocol names, here and in every other service block, are `claim_producer`, `executor`, `publisher`, `lifecycle_subscriber`, `validation`, and `data_processing`.

### named_locks

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `named_locks.<name>.limit` | int ≥ 1 | none — required | Capacity of a producer-independent counter. A limit of 1 is a mutex; above 1 is a counting semaphore. |

A template that names a lock literally must name one declared here, or registration fails.

### executors

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `executors.<name>.transport` | `grpc` \| `http` \| `inproc` | none — required | How the supervisor dispatches. `inproc` addresses executors running inside the rimsky process. |
| `executors.<name>.endpoint` | `host:port` under `grpc`; a URL under `http` | none — required | Where to dispatch. |
| `executors.<name>.tls` | `off` \| `required` | `off`, or `required` when `service_auth: mtls` | Under `transport: http`, `required` also demands an `https://` endpoint. |
| `executors.<name>.protocols` | list | `[executor]` | Must include `executor`. |
| `executors.<name>.observability_endpoint` | `host:port` | the entry's `endpoint` | Address of the executor-observability protocol when served separately. |

An executor named here overrides a bundled executor of the same name.

### publishers

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `publishers.<name>.endpoint` | `host:port` | none — required | Where to reach the sensor. |
| `publishers.<name>.tls` | `off` \| `required` | `off`, or `required` when `service_auth: mtls` | Verifies the service's server certificate. |
| `publishers.<name>.protocols` | list | `[publisher]` | Must include `publisher`. |
| `publishers.<name>.observability_endpoint` | `host:port` | the entry's `endpoint` | Address of the observability sibling. |

### validators

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `validators.<name>.endpoint` | `host:port` | none — required | Where to reach the validating service. |
| `validators.<name>.tls` | `off` \| `required` | `off`, or `required` when `service_auth: mtls` | Verifies the service's server certificate. |
| `validators.<name>.protocols` | list | `[validation]` | Must include `validation`. |
| `validators.<name>.observability_endpoint` | `host:port` | the entry's `endpoint` | Address of the observability sibling. |

Validators are consulted at template registration, never per dispatch.

### data_processors

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data_processors.<name>.endpoint` | `host:port` | none — required | Where to reach the data-processing service. |
| `data_processors.<name>.tls` | `off` \| `required` | `off`, or `required` when `service_auth: mtls` | Verifies the service's server certificate. |
| `data_processors.<name>.protocols` | list | `[data_processing]` | Must include `data_processing`. |
| `data_processors.<name>.observability_endpoint` | `host:port` | the entry's `endpoint` | Address of the observability sibling. |

### retention

Every value is a Go duration or a count. Setting one to 0 disables that sweep; a negative value fails at load.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `retention.recent_frames_kept` | int | `100` | Keeps this many most-recently-ended frames per instance; older ended frames are pruned with their node runs and attributes. |
| `retention.trace_trailing` | duration | `720h` | Prunes ended frames and event-log rows older than this. Combines with `recent_frames_kept`: a frame matching either bound is pruned. |
| `retention.lineage_trailing` | duration | `720h` | Deletes lineage records older than this. |
| `retention.claim_handles_trailing` | duration | `720h` | Deletes claim-handle rows older than this. |
| `retention.message_idempotencies_trailing` | duration | `24h` | Deletes message-idempotency rows older than this. |
| `retention.lifecycle_outbox_trailing` | duration | unset — nothing is discarded | Deletes lifecycle-outbox rows older than this, delivered or not. Unset keeps rimsky's at-least-once promise unconditional; a positive value is an operator's explicit decision to discard what a service has not acknowledged by that age. It must be longer than `service_delivery.stall_after`, so the stall signal reports the failure before the window discards it; a shorter window fails at load. |

### service_delivery

Deployment-wide tuning for delivery to services.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `service_delivery.stall_after` | duration | `5m` | How long a service's oldest pending outbox row may wait before rimsky calls that service stalled. It also caps the retry backoff, so a stalled service is retried no less often than the threshold that declares it stalled. Must be positive; a zero or negative value fails at load. |

### dispatch_defaults

Deployment-wide fallbacks for three of a node's dispatch deadlines. A node's own value wins where the node sets one.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dispatch_defaults.sync_rpc_deadline` | duration | unset — no default deadline | Deadline on the synchronous dispatch RPC. |
| `dispatch_defaults.max_quiet_period` | duration | unset | How long a dispatch may go without progress. Must be 0 or at least `1s`; a smaller positive value fails at load. |
| `dispatch_defaults.max_runtime` | duration | unset | Wall-clock ceiling on one dispatch. Must be 0 or at least `1s`. |

**Retry policy has no deployment-wide form, and guessing one stops the deployment.** These three keys are the whole block. Adding `max_retries` or any `retry_backoff` subkey under `dispatch_defaults` — the natural guess from the per-node timing keys — fails the migrate step with `field max_retries not found`, and the entrypoint reports `ENTRYPOINT.MIGRATE.FAILED`. Set retry policy on each node instead.

### late_bind_service_proxies

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `late_bind_service_proxies.<protocol>` | string | empty | Maps a protocol name to the service entry that fronts late-bound services for it. The keys rimsky consults are `executor` and `claim_producer`. |

An empty map leaves late-bind resolution inert: a dispatch to an unresolved name simply does not resolve.

### supervisor

Supervisor tuning. The supervisor role reads this section of `rimsky.yml`; there is no second file.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `supervisor.supervisor_id` | string | `<hostname>-<pid>` | Identifies this supervisor in the supervisor registry. |
| `supervisor.concurrency` | int | `4` | Dispatches in flight at once. A value below 1 is replaced by the default. |
| `supervisor.liveness_interval_ms` | int | `5000` | How often the supervisor refreshes its liveness. A value below 100 is replaced by the default. |
| `supervisor.claim_poll_interval_ms` | int | `1000` | How often the supervisor polls for claimable work. A value below 50 is replaced by the default. |
| `supervisor.callback.host` | string | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address of the async-callback listener. |
| `supervisor.callback.port` | int | `8081` | Bind port. 0 takes an operating-system-assigned port. |
| `supervisor.callback.advertise_host` | string | unset | Hostname stamped into callback URLs handed to executors. |
| `supervisor.callback.advertise_port` | int | the bound port | Port stamped into callback URLs. |

Note the three silent floors: a `concurrency` of 0, a `liveness_interval_ms` of 50, or a `claim_poll_interval_ms` of 10 does not take effect and does not warn — each is replaced by the default above.

`supervisor.callback.advertise_host` is the one key here that can stop startup. The listener binds `0.0.0.0` by default, which is not an address an executor can dial back on, so an unset advertise host over a wildcard bind is refused rather than stamped into callback URLs. Set it to a hostname the executors can reach. An explicit non-wildcard `supervisor.callback.host` serves as the advertise fallback. `RIMSKY_SUPERVISOR_CALLBACK_ADVERTISE_HOST` and `RIMSKY_SUPERVISOR_CALLBACK_ADVERTISE_PORT` override the two advertise keys, and take precedence over the file.

### service_auth

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `service_auth` | `none` \| `mtls` | `none` | Posture on the internal service-to-service boundary. |

Under `none`, internal dials are plaintext against a trusted-subnet assumption, and no certificate machinery runs. Under `mtls`, a per-deployment certificate authority issues short-lived leaf certificates, every standing service enrols, and both services of every internal leg present and verify certificates. `mtls` also flips the default `tls` mode on every service entry from `off` to `required`, and it requires `RIMSKY_CA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to hold a standard-base64 32-byte key; a missing or malformed key fails startup.

### unreachable_validator_policy

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unreachable_validator_policy` | `permissive_warn` \| `strict` | `permissive_warn` | What happens when a validating service cannot be reached during template registration. |

Under `permissive_warn` the registration succeeds and the unreachable validator surfaces as a warning. Under `strict` it surfaces as an error and the registration is rejected.

### What rimsky.yml does not configure

**There is no authentication toggle.** Anonymous mode — the state in which the api-key ledger holds no active rows — is derived from data, not set by configuration. Each of `anonymous_mode`, `auth`, `require_auth`, `anonymous`, and `auth_mode` stops the container at startup with `field <name> not found`, and the refusal prints the whole top-level schema: the fourteen keys above, none of them an auth switch. The environment offers no switch either. What the product gives instead is a warning banner while the ledger is empty, an immediate flip to enforcing the moment the first key is minted, and a guard on the way back that refuses to revoke the last key without an explicit force.

## CLI config

`rimsky` reads `~/.rimsky/config.yml`. `rimsky ctx` and `rimsky auth login` write it; the file is created with mode 0600 inside a 0700 directory.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `current_context` | string | empty | Names the context the CLI uses when no endpoint is given another way. |
| `contexts.<name>.endpoint` | URL | none | Control-API endpoint for that context. |
| `contexts.<name>.api_key` | string | empty | Bearer token for that context. |

A context name must start with a letter and may carry letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-`, up to 63 characters.

Endpoint resolution runs in order: `--endpoint`, then `RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL`, then a context pinned by a compose manifest, then the context named by `RIMSKY_CONTEXT`, then `current_context`. With none of those set, the command fails and names the three ways to fix it. The compose verbs reorder the first and third: a manifest's pinned context wins, and a `--endpoint` resolving to a different address than the pinned context fails with both values named. Key resolution runs `--key`, then `RIMSKY_API_KEY`, then the resolved context's `api_key`.

### Service aliases

Aliases are a separate file — `~/.rimsky/aliases.yml`, then `./.rimsky/aliases.yml`, with the working-directory file winning on a collision.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aliases.<name>` | path | none | Path `rimsky run --service <name>` spawns when the flag names no path. |

`--service <name>=<path>` bypasses aliases entirely. `--service <name>` with no alias defined fails and tells you to give the path.

## Bundled claim producers

Each bundled claim producer reads one YAML file, named by its own environment variable. With the variable unset, the service starts unconfigured and serves nothing.

Both producers open the same three listeners on the same `host`, and both take a `pick_policies` map whose keys are the selectors a template's claims name.

### claim-producer-filesystem

Config path: `RIMSKY_CLAIM_PRODUCER_FILESYSTEM_CONFIG`.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | path | none — required | Store root. Every pick policy's root resolves under it. |
| `host` | string | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address for all three listeners. |
| `grpc_port` | int | `9100` | Claim-producer gRPC port. |
| `http_port` | int | `9110` | HTTP bridge port. |
| `http_bridge_url` | URL | empty | Address the producer advertises for its HTTP bridge in its observability capabilities. |
| `admin_port` | int | `0` | Admin HTTP port. 0 mounts no admin listener. |
| `sweep_interval_seconds` | int | `60` | How often expired visibility timeouts are reclaimed. 0 takes the default. |
| `enable_lifecycle` | bool | `false` | Also serve the lifecycle-subscriber protocol. |
| `ledger_max_records` | int | `1024` | Size of the in-memory claim ledger the observability protocol reads. |
| `pick_policies.<name>.root` | relative path | store root | Subdirectory this policy picks from. An absolute path, or one escaping the store root, fails at load. |
| `pick_policies.<name>.folder_pattern` | regular expression | empty | Restricts picking to folder names that match. |
| `pick_policies.<name>.on_commit` | action | none — required | What happens to the folder on commit. |
| `pick_policies.<name>.on_give_up` | action | none — required | What happens to the folder on abandon. |
| `pick_policies.<name>.visibility_timeout_seconds` | int > 0 | none — required | How long an in-progress item stays invisible before the sweep reclaims it. |
| `pick_policies.<name>.sync_strategy` | `on_open` \| `on_drain` \| `explicit` \| `never` | `on_open` | When the policy rescans its root for new folders. |

An action is either a bare string — `pop`, `pop_and_delete`, or `recycle` — or a single-key map for the one action that takes a target: `{ pop_and_move: archive/ }`. A bare `pop_and_move` fails at load for want of a target, and a target on any other action fails too. The move target must stay inside the store root and on the same filesystem.

Two combinations are checked at load. `on_commit: pop` with `sync_strategy: on_open` is rejected, because the rescan would re-add every popped folder and the queue would never drain; use `on_drain`. `on_commit: recycle` with `sync_strategy: on_drain` is accepted with a warning that it is inert, because a recycling queue never empties and `on_drain` therefore never fires.

`sync_strategy: explicit` puts the rescan behind the admin listener, so it requires a non-zero `admin_port`; a policy asking for `explicit` without one fails at load and names the policy.

**The default `grpc_port` sits in the bundled-service block.** 9100 belongs to this producer alone: core listeners take 8080 through 8099 and the bundled services take 9000 through 9199, so the producer binds beside the core stack on one host at defaults. Give it `grpc_port` and `http_port` of your own when a second copy shares the host.

### claim-producer-postgres

Config path: `RIMSKY_CLAIM_PRODUCER_POSTGRES_CONFIG`.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `connection` | connection string | none — required | Postgres the producer serves claims from. |
| `write_semantics` | `sync` \| `staged_async` \| `blocking_async` \| `read_only` | `staged_async` | The value this producer realizes. An unrecognised value fails at load. |
| `host` | string | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address for all three listeners. |
| `grpc_port` | int | `9101` | Claim-producer gRPC port. |
| `http_port` | int | `9111` | HTTP bridge port. |
| `http_bridge_url` | URL | empty | Address advertised for the HTTP bridge in observability capabilities. |
| `admin_port` | int | `0` | Admin HTTP port. 0 mounts no admin listener. |
| `sweep_interval_seconds` | int | `30` | How often expired visibility timeouts are reclaimed. 0 takes the default. |
| `enable_lifecycle` | bool | `false` | Also serve the lifecycle-subscriber protocol. |
| `enable_executor` | bool | `false` | Also serve the executor protocol and its observability sibling. |
| `ledger_max_records` | int | `1024` | Size of the in-memory claim ledger the observability protocol reads. |
| `pick_policies.<name>.items_table` | SQL identifier | none — required | Table this policy picks rows from. Lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, not starting with a digit; anything else fails at load. |
| `pick_policies.<name>.on_commit` | `pop` \| `recycle` | none — required | What happens to the row on commit. `pop_and_move` and `pop_and_delete` are rejected. |
| `pick_policies.<name>.on_give_up` | `pop` \| `recycle` | none — required | What happens to the row on abandon. |
| `pick_policies.<name>.visibility_timeout_seconds` | int > 0 | none — required | How long a picked row stays invisible before the sweep reclaims it. |
| `partition_policies.<name>.items_table` | SQL identifier | none — required | Table the partition query runs against. |
| `partition_policies.<name>.select` | SQL select list | none — required | Columns the query returns. The first must be the row id. |
| `partition_policies.<name>.where` | SQL predicate | none — required | Filter. May carry `$1`, `$2` … placeholders. |
| `partition_policies.<name>.params_schema.properties` | mapping | empty | Declares the caller-supplied parameter names, in order. The declaration order binds the `$N` placeholders. |
| `partition_policies.<name>.limit` | int | `0` | Caps returned rows. 0 applies no limit. |

A `where` carrying `$N` placeholders with no `params_schema` fails at load: the ordering has to be declared, because an alphabetical fallback would bind arguments to the wrong placeholders without saying so. At call time, a parameter declared in `params_schema` but missing from the request is an error, as is a request supplying parameters against a policy that declared none.

## Publisher kinds

A publisher is declared in the template, not in a configuration file: `publishers[]` entries carry a `name` naming a service in `rimsky.yml`'s `publishers` block, a `kind`, a `message_type`, and a `config` block whose keys are the kind's own. The keys below are those `config` keys. The template's registration checks the `kind` against the named service's advertised kinds and rejects one it does not advertise.

Four kinds ship.

### cron

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cron` | standard cron expression | none — required | Schedule. An unparseable expression fails the subscription. |

Each firing sends one message carrying the observation time, the expression, the scheduled fire time, and a count of windows missed since the last firing. Missed windows coalesce into one message rather than replaying one per window. The idempotency key is the subscription plus the scheduled fire time, so two processes firing the same window deliver one message.

### http

Polls a URL and sends a message when the response body changes.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | URL | none — required | Poll target. |
| `poll_interval` | duration string | `30s` | How often to poll. Must be positive. |
| `match.status` | list of int | 2xx | Status codes that count as a hit. |
| `match.jsonpath.path` | dotted path | empty | Requires this path to exist in the JSON body. |
| `match.jsonpath.value` | string | empty | Requires the value at that path to equal this. Ignored when `path` is empty. |

A message goes out only when the response matches and its body hash differs from the last one sent. Bodies over 10 MiB are dropped with a warning. The poll goes through the outbound-egress guard, which blocks loopback, private, link-local, and multicast destinations unless the operator opens the range.

**The `http` kind takes no `auth` block, and writing one is accepted in silence.** Registration returns 201, deploy returns 200, the subscription mounts live — and then the sensor polls the upstream carrying no credential. Nothing warns at registration, at deploy, at subscribe, or in the sensor's log. The block is decoded into a struct without such a field and dropped. Only the `webhook` kind takes and enforces `auth`.

### object-store

Watches a bucket for new objects.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backend` | string | none — required | Which registered backend to list through. |
| `bucket` | string | none — required | Bucket to list. |
| `prefix` | string | empty | Restricts listing to object names with this prefix. |
| `poll_interval` | duration string | `30s` | How often to list. Must be positive. |
| `settle_window` | duration string | `0s` | Ignores objects modified more recently than this, so a partly-written object is not picked up. Must not be negative. |
| `watermark_field` | `name` \| `last_modified` | `name` | Which field orders the watermark that tracks progress. Any other value fails the subscription. |

**`backend` does not name a cloud object store.** The shipped build services two backends and both are local: `filesystem`, registered when the sensor is given a root directory, and `memory`, registered only when explicitly enabled. A publisher naming `s3`, `gcs`, or `azure` stays in `mounting` and never goes active; the reason appears only in the orchestrator's log, as `resolved_config.backend "s3" is not serviceable by this build (registered backends: filesystem)`. Under the filesystem backend, `bucket` is a subdirectory of the sensor's own root.

### webhook

Serves an inbound HTTP path and turns each accepted delivery into a message.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path_prefix` | path | none — required | Path this subscription serves. A leading `/` is added when absent. Two subscriptions cannot claim the same prefix. |
| `idempotency_header` | header name | empty | Header read as the delivery's idempotency key. Empty reads no header. |
| `auth.mode` | `hmac` \| `secret_header` \| `none` | none — required | Authentication scheme. The whole `auth` block is required; a subscription without one never mounts. |
| `auth.secret` | string | none — required under `hmac` and `secret_header` | Shared secret. |
| `auth.signature_header` | header name | `X-Rimsky-Signature` | Under `hmac`, the header carrying the signature. |
| `auth.timestamp_header` | header name | none — required under `hmac` | Header carrying the signed timestamp. Replay protection is mandatory, so `hmac` without it is rejected. |
| `auth.replay_window_seconds` | int ≥ 0 | `300` | Under `hmac`, how far a timestamp may sit from now. A negative value is rejected. |
| `auth.header` | header name | none — required under `secret_header` | Header carrying the secret. |

Under `hmac` the signature is `sha256=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp header value, a `.`, and the raw body. Under `secret_header` the named header must carry the secret. Either way a delivery presenting no credential is refused 401. When `idempotency_header` is set, a delivery repeating the immediately preceding key is accepted 200 and produces no message.
